title: Incident Record (share-2w)
description: Documents an incident injected via a feature flag, including its mechanism and observable symptoms across metrics, logs, traces, and frontend behavior. Applies to the share-2w dataset.
$comment: Serialize conforming files with ensure_ascii=False (raw UTF-8) so non-ASCII characters such as → and — are written directly rather than as \uXXXX escapes. Keeps the human-readable form in the file and makes diffs legible.

incident_time.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (with timezone) when the feature flag was toggled on.

feature_flag.description: Name of the flagd feature flag that was enabled.

description.description: Markdown-formatted summary of what the flag does and its user-facing effects.

mechanism.description: Markdown-formatted explanation of the code path from flag check to user-visible failure, with source file references as markdown links relative to the directory containing rendered markdown (share-2w/solutions/), e.g. [\`main.go#L485\`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/product-catalog/main.go#L485).

symptoms.description: Observable symptoms grouped by signal type.

metrics.description: Prometheus metrics that changed (spiked, dropped, flatlined) during the incident.

logs.description: Log patterns observed in OpenSearch during the incident.

frontend.description: User-perceived symptoms in the frontend — HTTP errors, timeouts, degraded performance, missing/stale content, or visual regressions.

traces.description: Distributed trace patterns observed in Jaeger during the incident.

metric.description: A metric family grouped by base name and exact label set, annotated with a signal layer and one or more variants.

metric_family.description: Base Prometheus metric name with histogram/summary suffixes stripped.

signal_layer.description: Causal position of this family in the incident chain.

defining_labels.description: Label key/value pairs shared by all variants in this family.

variants.description: Individual metric variants (e.g. _count, _sum) belonging to this family.

type.description: How the variant changed during the incident (e.g. created, collapsed, spiked, inconclusive). May include a '(fixed after human verification)' suffix.

query.description: PromQL query that surfaces this variant.

description.description: Human-readable description of the variant behavior.

onset_utc.description: UTC timestamp when the variant first deviated from baseline, or null if inconclusive.

onset_offset_seconds.description: Seconds between the incident time and the onset, or null if inconclusive.

onset_reasoning.description: Explanation of how the onset was determined, or null if inconclusive.

name.description: Short label for the log pattern. For HTTP access logs (e.g. Envoy, which have empty severity), use 'METHOD /path → status_code' (example: 'GET /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z → 500') — no severity suffix. For application logs that carry a non-empty severity, use '{service}: {summary} ({SEVERITY})' where SEVERITY is normalized to the canonical OTel uppercase level (INFO, WARN, ERROR, DEBUG, TRACE, FATAL) regardless of how the SDK serializes severity.text (.NET 'Information' → INFO, 'Warning' → WARN, 'Error' → ERROR; Python 'WARNING' → WARN; Go 'info' → INFO). Examples: 'ad: Feature Flag adManualGc enabled (WARN)', 'Recommendation: Cache Miss (INFO)', 'cart: Wasn''t able to connect to redis (ERROR)'. Omit the ({SEVERITY}) suffix if the log has no meaningful severity.

description.description: Time range and summary of the log pattern.

cause.description: Why this log pattern appeared — direct effect or cascading failure.

source.description: Originating service or log source (e.g. 'frontend-proxy Envoy access logs').

representative_attributes.description: Key attributes from a representative log entry. Keys are OpenTelemetry log attribute names.

body.description: The log record body — the main message text of the log entry.

resource.service.name.description: OTel resource attribute `service.name` identifying the service that emitted the log.

log_documents.description: References to specific OpenSearch log documents.

description.description: What the user sees — the symptom and the affected page / product / flow.

route.description: The HTTP route, UI page, or user flow affected (e.g. 'GET /api/products/[productId]', 'GET /', 'Cart page').

deterministic.description: True if the failure always occurs given the trigger condition; false if it depends on a random or conditional factor.

trigger_condition.description: The user action or system state that causes this failure.

symptom_type.description: Category of user-perceived symptom. http_5xx = server error response; http_4xx = client error; http_timeout = request hangs past deadline; slow_response = completes but with elevated latency; visual_degradation = page loads but a UI element is missing/broken; partial_content = page loads with some elements failed; stale_content = page loads with outdated/cached data.

source_file.description: Path (relative to opentelemetry-demo/) to the most relevant source file for this symptom. Optional when the symptom has no single call site.

source_line.description: Line number in source_file for the most relevant call site. Optional when the symptom has no single call site.

calling_service.description: The service whose behavior most directly produces the symptom.

call_pattern.description: How the affected call or operation is invoked — single call, parallel loop, deep-nested dependency, background retry, etc.

cause.description: Explanation of how the flag propagates to the user-visible symptom.

name.description: Short label for the trace pattern (e.g. 'Product Page Cascade').

description.description: Time range and summary of the trace pattern.

cause.description: Why this trace pattern appeared — direct effect or cascading failure.

call_chain.description: Service-level call chain from root cause to entry point, formatted as 'service:operation → service:operation → ...'.

smoking_gun.description: Span attributes, events, or logs that definitively tie this trace to the feature flag.

@timestamp.description: Timestamp of the log entry (HH:mm:ss.SSS format).

user_action.description: Load generator action that initiated this trace (e.g. 'user_browse_product').
